body:
## Problem

Some batches carry pairs that must not land separately: a caller-first rule ("no producer on the base without its consumer"), or two issues explicitly planned to "merge as one unit". Stack mode preserves this at the merge boundary — the maintainer merges the stack bottom-up and can take the pair together. Merge mode cannot: it merges **every** completed non-final wave at its boundary, and a chained pair (consumer builds on the merged producer) forces the producer onto the base a full build-cycle before the consumer — or indefinitely, if the flow stops between the two.

There is no per-bundle or per-pair control: `wave_mode` is global, and briefs have no way to say "hold this until X merges with it".

## Real-world context

getwyrd/wyrd-pdca's active alpha re-slicing plan has two such chained pairs (wyrd 635.6→636.5: "#653 is never merged without #658 stacked behind it"; wyrd #625→#633: "merge as one unit"). After switching the instance to merge mode (getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#198), the only options are folding each pair into a single over-budget bundle or pulling the pair out of the driver entirely and hand-stacking it. Both work; both give up part of what the harness is for.

## Proposal (sketch)

An atomic-group marker on the brief (e.g. `Merges with: #NNN`). In merge mode the driver holds a completed group member's PR (skips its `ready`+`merge`) until every member of the group is COMPLETE, then merges the group back-to-back in dependency order at one wave boundary — with the chained-pair case handled by letting the dependent build on the *unmerged* producer branch for exactly the held span (or by documenting that a chained atomic pair must be one bundle, and having the sizer/splitter refuse to split across such a boundary).
